We understand that Idaho has long considered a property tax limit modeled
on California's Proposition 13, and dramatic increases in property values have
reignited debate on assessment/tax limits. But we implore you, do we really
want to be akin to California?
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avefue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Property tax systems are established by state legislation, yet the
overwhelming majority of property tax revenue supports local government.
Setting the proposed limits in SB 1021 thus represents a restriction by one
level of government, the state, on the funds available to another, local
jurisdictions.
RE: SB 1021
Dear Honorable Senate Committee Members:

Members of the Senate Committee
on Local Government and Taxation
January 27, 2021

The time has come to put a stop to the proposed harsh limits in SB 1021,
which will put severe pressure over time on local governments' ability to
deliver the services that their residents expect and need, from schools and
police and fire protection to city parks and affordable housing
initiatives. Local jurisdictions will be forced to increase fees for services such
as sewerage, trash pick-up, community college classes, and participation in
school athletics or other extracurricular activities. Like sales taxes, fees
typically fall hardest on those with the least ability to pay.

On behalf of the Citizens of Payette, we strongly urge you to vote against SB
1021.

Jeffrey f. Williams
Payette's Mayor

The limits proposed in SB 1021, are a deeply flawed means to counter rising
property taxes. They are offered in hope of reducing tax bills and slowing the shift in
tax burdens to residential property, but in fact they can result in higher taxes for the
very homeowners they are intended to assist and can cause unpredictable new
shifts in tax liabilities. Implementing the tax limits in SB 1021 will impose widely
differing tax obligations on owners of identical properties, reduce economic growth
by distorting taxpayer decision making, and greatly reduce the transparency and
accountability of the property tax system as a whole.

Not only will local jurisdictions be forced to cut services and increase fees, but this
bill will also severely hamstring our ability to foster economic development and
future growth. The best tax policy for our local jurisdictions seeking to grow our
economies are those that offer long-term certainty to businesses and individuals
and designed with the principles of efficiency, simplicity, and equity in mind. Smart
tax policies, which are not based on political whim such as SB 1021, also have the
best chance of promoting fairness across the board.
City of Payette ~ 700 Center Avenue ~ Payette, ID 83661 ~ 208-642-6024

Again, we respectfully urge you to keep Idaho prosperous and vote against SB 1021.
We do not want to be another California!
Sincerely,
CITY OF PAYETTE
January 22, 2021
Friday Legislative Update

This week saw the introduction of the property tax cap legislation that is sponsored by members of
the legislative Property Tax Working Group. Senate Bill 1021 would have a terrible impact on Idaho's
future economic growth and job creation, by forcing cities to tightly restrict residential and
commercial development, which is the engine of our state's economy and a primary revenue driver
for the sales and income taxes that fund state and local government. The bill is expected to be up for
a hearing in the Senate Local Government & Taxation Committee on Wednesday, January 27 or
Thursday, January 28 in the afternoon.

This week has been incredibly busy from the perspective of AIC staff having meetings, reviewing and
analyzing bills and working cooperatively with other local government association partners to
advocate before the Legislature.

By restricting local governments' ability to fund the services and infrastructure needed to serve
growth through the new construction levy, that tax burden will be shifted to current residents. If

The Legislature knows the answer to the problem and continues to refuse to pass legislation to raise
and/or index the homeowner's exemption or increase relief for elderly, disabled, widows and
disabled veterans through the circuit breaker.

The legislation is based on the disproved idea that local government property tax levies, not rapidly
rising residential values that are outstripping ag and commercial property values, are the policy
problem that needs addressed. As the Legislature has heard numerous times, even the property tax
freeze bill from last session would have still seen homeowners in rapidly growing areas paying more
in taxes because their property values are increasing so much faster than other classes of property.

For cities where new construction roll value constitutes less than 2% growth in the taxing district's
budget, the taxing district may choose either: (A) an increase including the highest dollar levy of the
previous three years, plus a growth factor for CPI that cannot exceed 3%, plus a growth factor
determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction and annexation
during the previous calendar year; or (B) the taxing district may choose a 3% increase.
Property Tax Cap: Senate Bill 1021

For cities that are growing, the property tax budget increase may be up to a maximum of 4% annually
(without voter approval for a temporary override of up to 2 years in duration with simple majority
voter approval or a permanent override approved by two-thirds of voters), plus: an increase including
the highest dollar levy of the previous three years, a growth factor for CPl that cannot exceed 3%, and
a growth factor determined by applying the prior year's levy rate to the value of new construction
and annexation during the previous calendar year, plus any forgone that the city chooses to capture.
The bill would make changes to the 3% Cap law as follows:

Legislation to divert $800,o00 from the State Liquor Account for funding the Peace Officers Standards
and Training Program (POsT) was introduced this week. House Bill 30, would split the amount equally
between the state and local governments. The AlC Board of Directors voted this week to oppose the
legislation because taking local government revenue, at a time when legislators are demanding that
cities provide property tax relief, will only add to the burden on city service funding. The state has a
massive revenue surplus that could have easily paid for this relatively small amount from the state
budget. Local governments were forced to the table to renegotiate the State Liquor Account
distribution formula during the Great Recession and local governments were forced to take a lower
share of future revenues as a result. AlC's lobbyists will be working this issue to let legislators know
of our opposition.

"Cities need to take a look at hitting the pause button on new development projects," said AIC
Legislative Chair Mayor John Evans of Garden City, "until we have a better understanding of the
impacts of this legislation. It would be irresponsible to allow development to happen that might
burden our existing property taxpayers with subsidizing new growth that they can't afford to pay."

local governments can't fund the police, firefighters, street maintenance, and other work that results
from new development, then local governments have no choice but to strictly curtail
development. This will hurt the state's economy and job creation, as well as state and local revenues
as significant portions of state sales and income tax revenues are derived from construction and
development.

We ask city officials to please contact their local legislators as soon as possible and respectfully ask
that they oppose Senate Bill 1021. Provide examples of development proposals that could be
affected and the economic impact to your community. Cities also need to work closely with
economic development agencies, chambers of commerce, building contractors, realtors and others to
advance the message about how devastating this legislation would be to Idaho's economy. AlC has
spoken with AGC, IBCA, the FOP, PFFI, Idaho Power, Simplot and many other organizations about the
potential harm to development and growth and welcomes your help in these important discussions.
Reach out to Legislators to Ask them to Oppose HB 16 on Disaster Emergencies

Another bill introduced this week would give the Idaho Legislature sweeping powers to modify or end
local disaster declarations made by cities and counties. House Bill 16 would be an unprecedented
state takeover of local disaster emergencies that are usually non-controversial and used to respond to
floods, mudslides, fires and other emergency situations. Please reach out to your legislators and let
them know that their locally elected city and county officials have been perfectly capable of managing
these situations without the state's involvement and that the unintended consequences and
potential loss of federal disaster funding is unacceptable.

Lopez stated that the Federal Government passed a law saying 21 is the legal age to
purchase tobacco. He as a retailer can get fined by the Federal Government if he
follows the State law of 18. For him as retailer it protects the retailers in the City to
change the Ordinance to 21.

City Attorney Chadwick let the Council know that the Ordinance can be raised to the
more stringent than state law to the age of 21 or even to 19 and it would be enforceable,
however, State Code does not allow for the City to make the Ordinance lower than the
State Law. Chief Plaza added that he would like to stay with the State Code as it adds
to more confusion to the officers if we change to something other than State Code.

Wickersham assumed we are doing this to follow State Code, is that the idea behind
this? Wickersham asked what brought this up?
Mayor Williams stated that Councilor
Lopez brought this to our attention as needing fixed.

A motion was made by Lopez and seconded by
Patrick to read Ordinance #1487 by title only.

Wickersham stated when you stop to think about this the entire state of Oregon and
California sell marijuana when the Federal law says you can't sell marijuana. Lopez
replied that the Federal government has every opportunity to fine the retailer.
Wickersham asked Lopez so as a retailer do you have the right to tell someone who is
18 that you will not sell to them? Lopez stated yes, I do have the right and the majority
of us (retailers in the City) do not sell to anyone under 21.

After a unanimous voice vote by the Council, the
motion CARRIED.

After a unanimous voice vote by the Council, the
motion CARRIED.
Mayor Williams read Ordinance #1487 by title only.

Chadwick stated there are two issues going on here. Do you as a City have a problem
with the sale of tobacco or vaping products to underage customers and how do you
actually manage that. If you need to increase the age you certainly can. The other part
has to do with if you are going to have a City Ordinance and a State Code you will want
to enforce the one which generates more revenue for the City. That way you are able to
fund the operations you are required to provide. Chadwick suggested to keep the
ordinance on the books so that the police can cite the City Code to generate that
revenue for the City.

Mayor Williams asked Lopez if this is a problem that is going on or just something
brought up? Lopez answered that he did not think it's a problem - just a house keeping
matter. Mayor Williams asked if we want our Police to oversee this or more pertinent
matters. Steiniker stated that maybe if we change the ordinance up to 21 than kids may
have a harder time getting ahold of tobacco products. Lopez asked do we really need to
have it in a City Ordinance if the State already has it? As Plaza stated he can enforce a
State Code. The question today is do we raise the Ordinance to align with the Federal
or just get rid of the Ordinance all together?

Kee stated he is always going to lean towards getting rid of ordinances we do not need.
In the old days' ordinances were based on revenues; if the police wrote a ticket on the
City ordinance than the City gets the revenue, if written on a State code the state gets
the revenue.

MAYORS COMMENTS

Jensen asked to address the concern of the water/sewer infrastructure. The previous
eight years that he was on City Council he never once questioned the budget for the
water/sewer department, which is fee based. He stated he always knew our rates were
good, so whatever they asked, in fact he can't remember anyone else on the Council
questioning their proposed budget. The only time I questioned the budget is when we
had another Council member ask why the rates were not going up again this year as it
is something we always do? Jensen stated why would we raise them if the departments
aren't asking for it in their budget? We don't just arbitrarily raise it because it is a new
year, let's as a council not raise it if the departments do not want it. His concern was
that the rates didn't need to be raised every year unless
they were asked for. Jensen
also stated that the one thing that would really help the City is to get the pool up and
running as soon as possible.

develop the annual budget for Council consideration and to provide Council with a
succinct method of articulating to staff the policy direction for the City of Payette, both
as a community and an organization. This strategic plan will also communicate to
residents and community partners the City Council's commitment to open government,
communication, collaboration, and cooperation among all who live, work, recreate,
educate, or operate a business in Payette.

STRATEGIC PLANNING PROPOSAL

Galena Consulting has over twenty years' experience in directing planning processes for agencies
in the public sector:

Our specific experience in strategic, operations, and capital planning for local governments
throughout the West ensures Payette will receive a strategic plan that reflects the policy
objectives of the elected officials, department leaders, community members and other
stakeholders.

Our specific experience conducting Payette's 2009 and 2016 strategic planning processes,
and developing impact fees for the City of Payette gives us a unique perspective on the needs
of the City.

Our specific experience in local government budget development and analysis ensures that
the Payette will receive a strategic plan that is reflective of the fiscal realities of the
community, and identifies the budget initiatives and/or alternatives that must be included in
future adopted budgets to realize the vision and objectives of the plan.
Introduction

Galena Consulting is uniquely qualified to facilitate a strategic planning process for the City of
Payette that clearly identifies the City's mission, goals, and objectives; aligns with the City's
annual budget planning processes; and sets forth specific action steps for the realization of the
City's goals and objectives.

Our specific experience in work planning and performance management ensures Payette will
receive a strategic plan that is actionable and measurable — clearly defining the steps that will
be taken by each department to realize the City's vision over a defined period of time.

Payette is a unique organization which supports a unique city. Rather than the application of a
template, this plan will be flexible and responsive to the distinctive needs of the City.

Strategic Planning Work Session — Consultant will facilitate a strategic planning work session
with elected officials and staff (3-4 hours) informed by the information gathering and public
involvement phases of the project. This will be followed by an action planning work session
with elected officials and staff (3-4 hours) to develop specific action steps necessary to
achieve the desired goals and objectives set forth in the strategic planning session.

Galena Consulting can begin to facilitate the update of Payette's strategic plan in February 2021.
The actual timeline of the proposed scope of work will depend on the availability of elected
officials and staff.

Review and Adoption of Strategic Action Plan — Consultant will facilitate the review and
adoption of the strategic plan by the Mayor and City Council Members.

Information Gathering - Staff - Consultant will interview city staff to assess the status of
2016 Strategic Plan and gather additional information about the City's current condition to
enhance the planning process. Specific attention will be spent evaluating current facilities
and services, and future service delivery needs.

Public Involvement — Consultant will engage the community in the strategic planning
process through a survey of community members to determine their concerns and priorities
for the City of Payette. Surveys would be conducted in an electronic format, collecting
data anonymously. This survey tool could be repeated at a later date as a benchmark to
determine the progress being made within the Strategic Action Plan. *Alternatively, or in
addition, Consultant can conduct a community open house to gather public input.
Scope of Work

Information Gathering — Elected Officials — Consultant will hold individual interviews with
the Mayor and members of the City Council to assess current issues and priorities.

Project Planning - Consultant will meet with point of contact for the City of Payette to
clarify project deliverables and timelines.

Galena Consulting ("Consultant") welcomes the opportunity to support the City of Payette as it
articulates its vision for the future of the City. This vision will build on protecting the qualities
dear to the community, while determining ways to capitalize on its economic development
potential in order to remain fiscally healthy and sustainable. Priorities will be set around
establishing service levels that respond to citizen expectations, while balancing policies around
